NDT training in Tulsa: how it works for Tulsa employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for Tulsa-area employers and technicians. We have no Tulsa classroom. Theory runs live online or in scheduled cohorts, and practical training runs onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight. Certification is granted by your employer under its written practice.

Tulsa's inspection economy is unusual because it combines three industries that rarely share a city. There is the oil and gas business that gave Tulsa its old nickname: refining, midstream headquarters, pipelines and the crude hub at Cushing an hour to the west. There is aviation maintenance and aerostructures, anchored by one of the largest airline maintenance bases in the world. And there is an equipment fabrication base, including heat exchangers, pressure vessels, compressors and oilfield equipment, much of which ships out through the Tulsa Port of Catoosa. Each of these sectors uses NDT every day, but under different codes and often different qualification schemes.

For a technician, that means choosing methods with care. A UT Level II from a pipeline contractor and a UT Level II from an aviation MRO are both real qualifications, but the specific examinations, procedures and codes behind them differ. For employers, it means your written practice and training programme have to fit your actual work, not a generic template. This page sets out how SNT-TC-1A training fits each part of the Tulsa market.

For dates and delivery options, request a Tulsa training quote. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Tulsa

Courses follow SNT-TC-1A topical outlines and document classroom hours for your written practice. The table shows typical Tulsa uses for each method. It is a guide to local demand, not a statement of any employer's requirements.

MethodLevelsWhat Tulsa employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, III prepWeld examination on fabricated pressure vessels and exchanger headers, refinery thickness monitoring, pipeline wall-loss assessmentNone for Level I; Level II requires Level I plus documented experience
PAUT (phased array)II, III prepFabrication-shop weld examination in place of RT, pipeline girth welds, corrosion mapping at refineries and compressor stationsUsually UT Level II per the written practice
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, III prepThick-wall vessel and header welds from Tulsa fabricators, crack sizingUsually UT Level II
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, III prepPipeline girth-weld radiography, shop radiography of pressure-vessel welds, castingsNone for Level I; Oklahoma radiographer certification is separate and required to handle sources
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, III prepOilfield equipment and drill-string components, structural and lifting equipment, fabrication weld inspectionNone for Level I
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, III prepAerospace components and non-magnetic alloys, stainless exchanger tubes-to-tubesheet weldsNone for Level I
VT (visual testing)I, II, III prepWeld visual on fabricated equipment and pipelines, refinery external surveys, structural inspectionNone for Level I
ET (eddy current)I, II, III prepAircraft structure and engine component surface-crack inspection, exchanger tubing at refineriesNone for Level I

UT covers more of Tulsa's work than any other method. Fabrication shops need it for weld examination on vessels built to ASME Section VIII. Refineries need it for thickness monitoring. Pipeline operators need it for integrity work. Level I covers theory, straight-beam thickness and calibration. Level II adds angle-beam weld examination, evaluation to code acceptance criteria and reporting.

PAUT and TOFD have grown quickly in fabrication. Many pressure-equipment buyers now accept encoded ultrasonic examination in place of radiography, because it avoids radiation exclusion zones in the shop and produces a permanent data record. Both courses assume UT Level II and cover scan planning, focal laws, encoded data collection and analysis.

RT remains central to pipeline construction and much shop work. The course covers exposure techniques, film and digital imaging, image quality indicators and interpretation. Oklahoma's separate radiographer certification is covered below.

ET and PT matter more in Tulsa than in most oil towns because of aviation. Airline maintenance and aerostructures work uses eddy current for surface and near-surface cracks around fastener holes and on engine and landing-gear components, and PT on non-ferrous parts. Aviation employers often qualify NDT personnel under NAS 410 or the airline industry's own specification, so check with your employer's Level III how SNT-TC-1A classroom hours will be credited. MT and VT are everyday methods in oilfield equipment manufacture and repair.

For Level III candidates, see ASNT Level III exam preparation. All courses are listed at NDT training programmes.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Tulsa, step by step

SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based. Whether you work for a pipeline contractor out of Tulsa, a vessel fabricator in Sapulpa or Catoosa, or a refinery inspection contractor, the steps are the same.

  1. Your employer's written practice governs. It lists the methods and levels certified, training and experience minimums, examination rules, the responsible Level III and recertification requirements. Fabricators working under ASME code programmes find their authorised inspection agency will expect NDT personnel to be qualified to a written practice that meets the relevant ASME Section V requirements.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Atlantis delivers this online, in cohorts or onsite. Required hours come from your written practice, normally based on SNT-TC-1A's recommended minimums. Refer to the training requirements matrix.
  3. Accumulate logged on-the-job experience. Experience must be in the method and at the level sought, documented and verified. Pipeline construction seasons and shop production runs both build hours, if they are recorded properly.
  4. Pass general, specific and practical examinations. General tests method theory. Specific tests your employer's procedures, equipment and codes, such as ASME Section V and VIII, API 1104 or the applicable aerospace specification. Practical is performed on real specimens and graded by or under a Level III.
  5. Pass the vision examination. Near-vision and colour contrast, at the frequency set in the written practice.
  6. Receive employer certification. Signed by the employer's certifying authority, usually on the Level III's recommendation.
  7. Recertify on schedule. Within the written practice's interval, with vision tests kept current in the meantime.

See the SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide for detail on changing employers, crediting prior experience and recertification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Tulsa crews

Atlantis has no physical training centre in Tulsa. There are three delivery routes.

  • Live online theory. Real-time instructor-led classes for the classroom portion. These suit pipeline technicians travelling between spreads and shift workers at refineries and MRO hangars. See NDT training online.
  • Classroom cohorts. When enough candidates need the same course, held at an arranged venue.
  • Onsite at your facility. At your fabrication shop, service company yard or plant, using your equipment, procedures and representative specimens. For Tulsa fabricators, practical sessions on real production weld geometries are far more useful than generic plates.

Scheduling in Tulsa usually follows three calendars. Refinery turnarounds are planned well in advance. Pipeline construction is seasonal and weather-driven. Fabrication shops follow order backlogs. We generally run theory online during busy periods and book onsite practical sessions and examinations for the gaps, such as the slower weeks between pipeline spreads or after a shop delivers a large order. Tell us when your people are available, and we will plan around it.

Ask about onsite training for your Tulsa crew. For larger programmes, see corporate NDT training.

Where NDT technicians work in Tulsa

Refining. HF Sinclair operates the Tulsa refinery complex on the west bank of the Arkansas River. Refinery mechanical integrity programmes rely on API 510, 570 and 653 inspection, with NDT performed to ASME Section V. Turnarounds bring surges of UT, PAUT, RT and ET work.

Midstream and pipelines. Tulsa is headquarters to major midstream operators including ONEOK, which absorbed Magellan Midstream, and Williams. The Cushing crude storage and pipeline hub is roughly an hour west. Pipeline construction and integrity work runs on API 1104 for welding and inspection, under federal pipeline safety regulations at 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. Operators' qualification programmes and contractors' written practices both come into play. Tank farms at Cushing and elsewhere generate API 653 tank work.

Aviation MRO and aerostructures. American Airlines' Tulsa maintenance base is one of the largest airline maintenance facilities in the world, and Tulsa also has aerostructures manufacturers and repair specialists such as NORDAM. Aviation NDT is heavily ET, PT, UT and MT on airframe, engine and component work. Some local employers qualify personnel under NAS 410 or the airline industry specification rather than SNT-TC-1A, so aviation-bound candidates should ask which scheme applies before they enrol.

Fabrication and manufacturing. The Tulsa area has a large concentration of heat-exchanger, pressure-vessel and process-equipment manufacturers, including air-cooled heat-exchanger makers, many working under ASME code programmes with their own quality systems. The Tulsa Port of Catoosa, at the head of the McClellan-Kerr Arkansas River Navigation System, lets fabricators ship oversized modules by barge. This is steady, year-round weld-inspection work in UT, PAUT, RT, MT and PT.

Infrastructure. Oklahoma DOT bridges, including large Arkansas River crossings, and structural steel for commercial construction bring VT, MT and UT work to AWS D1.1 and D1.5.

Radiography licensing in Oklahoma. Oklahoma is an NRC Agreement State. The Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality, Radiation Management Section, licenses radioactive materials use and certifies industrial radiographers in the state, with rules in Oklahoma Administrative Code Title 252, Chapter 410. Certification requires radiation-safety training, documented supervised experience and a state examination. Out-of-state licensees can work in Oklahoma under reciprocity. Your company's radiation safety officer handles licensing, but individual radiographers carry their own certification.

Level III services and written practices for Tulsa NDT companies

Tulsa has many mid-sized fabricators and service companies that perform NDT as part of production or field work but do not employ a full-time Level III. Their written practice is often years old, drafted for one method and then stretched to cover others. That becomes a problem when an authorised inspector, a pipeline operator or a customer's quality auditor starts asking questions.

  • Written practice development. We write or revise your written practice for the methods you actually perform, including PAUT and TOFD, and align it with the current SNT-TC-1A edition and the ASME, API or AWS requirements your customers name. See written practice development.
  • Outside Level III services. Examination administration, procedure and technique approval, and certification-record audits.
  • Audit preparation. Review of training records, experience logs, vision tests and exam results before code or customer audits.

Book a Level III consultation for your Tulsa company, or read the SNT-TC-1A guidance.

Practise before the practical exam

Candidates usually fail practical exams on process rather than knowledge: skipped calibration checks, poor scanning coverage, or recording and sizing errors. The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Tulsa, the welding workshop suits fabrication, the hangar suits aviation MRO and the oil and gas and tank environments suit refinery and midstream work.

The simulator is for practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens under a Level III. For written exams, try our UT Level 2 practice questions and the related sets.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop builds course content to SNT-TC-1A topical outlines and oversees practical sessions and examinations as the responsible Level III. Tulsa employers arranging onsite programmes plan them directly with him.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Tulsa

How do I get NDT certified in Tulsa?

Pick a method Tulsa employers use, with UT, MT or RT for oil and gas and fabrication, or ET and PT for aviation. Complete formal Level I training, gain logged experience and pass your employer's general, specific and practical examinations plus a vision test. Your employer then certifies you under its written practice.

Can I take NDT training online in Oklahoma?

Yes, the classroom portion can be taken through live online classes. Practical training and exams must be hands-on, so online theory is paired with onsite practical work. See NDT training online.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which normally follows SNT-TC-1A's recommended classroom and experience hours. Classroom training is the shorter part. Experience takes longer and depends on your workload. See the training requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Oklahoma?

Yes. The Oklahoma DEQ Radiation Management Section licenses radiography companies and certifies industrial radiographers. That requires radiation-safety training, supervised experience and a state exam. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is a separate NDT credential, and you need both.

What does NDT training cost in Tulsa?

We do not publish prices. Cost depends on method, level, group size and delivery. Request a Tulsa training quote and you will receive a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Tulsa employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the dominant framework for Tulsa's refining, pipeline and fabrication employers. Some aviation employers use NAS 410 or an airline industry specification instead. SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based, so a new employer recertifies you under its own written practice.

Can Atlantis training help me get into aviation NDT in Tulsa?

Our ET, PT, UT and MT courses cover method fundamentals that aviation employers value. Whether the hours count toward an aviation employer's NAS 410 or airline-scheme certification is that employer's Level III's decision, so ask before enrolling.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Tulsa?

No. We deliver live online theory, cohorts at arranged venues and onsite training at your facility.

Can you train our fabrication shop's inspectors on PAUT?

Yes, provided they hold UT Level II or your written practice allows another route. Onsite practical sessions can use your own weld mock-ups and production geometries.

Do you offer API 1104, API 510 or CWI courses?

No. Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Our RT and UT courses cover the NDT methods used on API 1104 pipeline work, but API inspector certifications and AWS CWI come through their own schemes.

Is pipeline NDT work seasonal in Oklahoma?

Construction work tends to follow weather and project cycles, while refinery, fabrication and MRO work runs year-round. Many Tulsa technicians hold methods that let them move between these sectors.

How do I prepare for ASNT Level III?

Use our Level III exam preparation for the Basic and method exams.
